tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find).

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

New `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents the styling-source hierarchy, unit rules, the alias-is-a-reference-not-a-copy principle, and a real gotcha: importing an already-overridden component via the SFCC base path resolves correctly in the real app but silently renders the unstyled base version in Storybook/Vitest (the `ccExtensibility` resolver is webpack-only, neither tool loads it). Still open, flagged inline rather than silently resolved: `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px prototype values) disagree with the Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px); `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all — both pending UI-designer sign-off.

  - **Committed & pushed (PR #61 as of 2026-08-25)**: Zephyr test case `SFCC-T285`, the site-prefix spec,

    Playwright projects — see `.docs/memory/feedback.md`), `MobileDrawerMenuPage.js` (new POM), the
    consent-dialog race-condition fix in `BasePage.dismissConsent()`, doc updates to
    `.claude/rules/testing.md` / `.claude/skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md` / `e2e/features/README.md`, and a
    second round of CodeRabbit-prompted fixes (consent-check caching per browser context, terminal-only
    BrowserStack status mapping, a `workflow_run` script-injection fix in `zephyr-results-sync.yml`).
  - **Real product gap found** (not a testing bug): the mobile hamburger drawer has zero category
    navigation links — matches an already-documented discrepancy against HPC-018 in

  - **Secrets live in GH Actions** (pushed 2026-08-24/25): `ZEPHYR_API_KEY`, `ZEPHYR_API_URL`,

## What's Pending
- All integrations need to point to production accounts (SFCC, Contentful)
- Global-e integration (confirm pricing flow mechanism before implementing)
- Didomi consent management (implement per storefront defaults in REG-054)
- Omneo / Emarsys marketing sync
- Adyen payment integration
- MuleSoft middleware connections
- PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout flows
- BOPIS (Collect in Boutique) checkout flow
- Full multi-site routing — 8 SFCC sites across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME). **US site topology updated (REG-005, 2026-07-10):** US splits into two separate SFCC sites — US domestic (`/us/`, SFCC checkout) and US international (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout). New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
- Address autocomplete via Google Maps API
- Narvar EDD + tracking integration
- SEO: hreflang, canonical URLs, sitemaps
- Order-on-behalf (OOBO) for CS agents
- Retail Rewards (AP21) integration
- Gift card PDP, cart, checkout, and GiveX integration
- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:
- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).
- Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD).
- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction (TBD).
- **Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (ENH-004, Must-Have, Go-Live) as SFCC OOTB configuration only. **Hard dependency:** Apple and Google merchant accounts must be provisioned by Zimmermann before implementation can start. Do not implement until merchant accounts exist.
- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.
- **Denmark routing:** Which storefront Denmark resolves to is not yet confirmed.
- **EU billing fields:** Locale-specific billing fields (Italian Codice Fiscale, Spanish NIF, French SIRET) — to be confirmed before implementing.

- **Optimizely SFCC data-layer scope (AAB-004):** Load mechanism Confirmed (PWA-direct head tag, US-only, Zimmermann-provided script). Residual: Tell No Lies suspects no SFCC-side data-layer work is needed for Optimizely (Magento launch was GTM-only). Confirm with Tell No Lies before doing SFCC data-layer work specifically for Optimizely.
- **CRM-155 customer group precedence:** Rules for resolving overlapping customer group memberships are TBD.

Confirm which sheet is authoritative before relying on Einstein for cart/recommendation surfaces.
- **PRC-45 Retail Rewards count per order:** Requirement text says "maximum of one Retail Reward per order" but RJ challenges: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order." Downgraded to Open — confirm the cap before building reward-application logic.
- **Addingwell role in analytics (AAB-001/003):** AAB-001 frames all container/tag logic as living in GTM (Tell No Lies), while the Third Party Integrations rows say the GTM container loads *via the Addingwell MRT integration* and GA4/downstream tags route through an Addingwell *server-side container*. Reconciled in analytics.md as logic-vs-transport, but confirm with Tell No Lies whether Addingwell is none / transport-only / server-side routing.
- **DMU-007 order history source (upstream):** DMU-007 PWA contract Confirmed (displays MuleSoft payload). Residual upstream conflict: requirement + JT say NewStore via MuleSoft; RJ says "Order history will come from Omneo." Out of PWA boundary — reconcile so the integration contract is unambiguous.
- **DMU-009 Contentful setup ownership:** RJ: "This is no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful." Downgraded pending reconciliation of who owns CMS setup.
- **Customer migration shape (DMU-004):** Only email + Omneo ID migrated; name, phone, addresses, comms prefs sourced **live from Omneo at login**. My Account profile pages must round-trip to Omneo post-auth. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages on account screens is now load-bearing — confirm UX before implementing profile reads.
- **Asset/CDN migration & platform (DMU-010 / DMU-020):** Asset migration de-scoped — no asset 301s; images stay in Contentful. Separately, the source note now records the platform CDN as Akamai (SFCC default), which sits against existing Cloudflare carry-forward references — confirm the CDN platform of record (no asset-migration impact either way).
- **PRC-43 Global-e cartridge customer-group catalogue prices:** Open with Global-e — does the cartridge honour customer-group catalogue prices (VIC) at international checkout? Also: how do VIC customers currently receive discounts at Global-e checkout in M2? Do not assume VIC pricing flows through Global-e until confirmed.
- **CFD-070 guest account creation flow:** Dependent on the guest journey design — open.
- **CFD-045 BOPIS seeding mechanism:** Open — how Collect in Boutique availability is seeded into checkout still TBC.
- **PAY-022 Adyen CVC config:** Confirm CVC-on-saved-card configuration with Adyen. PWA behaviour (re-entry required) is Confirmed.
- **PAY-047/048/049 fraud hold scope:** Adyen/NewStore-owned per IC; PWA-side display behaviour not yet signed off.
- **OM-002 MuleSoft order export gating:** Sign-off pending on the exact attribute set passed at order export.
- **OM-017/018 NewStore order status taxonomy:** SFCC displays raw MuleSoft status; mapping list still open.
- **OM-034 back-in-stock FIFO email logic:** Sign-off pending.
- **DLV-012 free-shipping thresholds:** Per-delivery-method per-storefront rate card updated; re-sign-off pending.
- **CAI-041 location-aware boutique inventory fallback:** Flagged as potential enhancement (RJ 25.05) — not in launch scope until confirmed.
- **RRC-030 tax/duties display location:** Confirm whether tax/duties appear in My Account vs Narvar/Global-e portals only.
- **CRM-022 international Retail Rewards via Global-e:** Not scoped; needs Global-e discussion.
- **CRM-048 / CRM-100 saved-address cap:** RJ proposes 20; IC "we can do this" — working target 20, formal sign-off pending.

Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.

  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.

=== feedback.md ===
*This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*

## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)

- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
  runs its tests."
- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
  skipped) regardless of its title.
- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.

**Resuming from:** SFCC-83/84 Recently Viewed — the rail plus the Full History page. The two E2E jobs show `skipping`, which is expected, not a failure: change-scoped E2E resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` when the diff spans shared paths no single area owns.

## Blockers and outstanding issues

- **Einstein is the real blocker behind SFCC-83/84.** Verified in BM 2026-09-07: Einstein shows "Not Deployed" on all 8 sites across 3 sandboxes, DNT defaults ON, and the siteId is still the `aaij-MobileFirst` demo value. Three stacking blockers, platform-wide rather than specific to this story. SFCC-112 is Blocked on it, and the standing note is **never enable Einstein on SIT**. Worth knowing before anyone treats Recently Viewed as end-to-end verifiable.
- **Four confirmed review defects still unposted.** Your own reviews confirmed them and they were never put on the PRs — re-verified live today. QA independently re-found four others as SFCC-898.
- **`projectState.md` is stale** (last updated 2026-08-24). Its "In Progress" section covers SFCC-55 footer, header refinement, and SFCC-751 — SFCC-83/84 isn't in it at all.
- **Sprint position contradicts itself.** `sprintScope.md` still says "Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress)" under Current position, while its own table puts Sprint 6 at 7–11 Sep, and Jira ground truth has Sprint 5 running to 21 Sep. Flagging rather than resolving — three sources, three answers.
- **Health checks:** `healthCheckAll.sh` ran but every target skipped (Digital SIT, OMS-INT, MuleSoft STG — no URLs in `.env.local`). 0 passed, 0 failed, 3 skipped, so it proved nothing either way.

## Ready when you are

Done. Both halves are complete.

## What I changed

**Fetched everything with prune** — 3 deleted remote refs cleaned up (`SFCC-737_pdp-product-content`, `SFCC-742_wishlist-loginpanel-content`, `sfcc-731-pdp-gallery`).

**Fast-forwarded local `develop`** — it was 178 commits behind (`a18c68be` → `3cec6380`). Confirmed clean fast-forward first (no local commits on it), and did it via `git fetch origin develop:develop` rather than checking it out, so there was never a moment where `develop` was the working branch.

**Created 6 local tracking branches** for remote branches that had none:

```
feature/SFCC-102_pdp-ui-slide-out-size-fit
feature/SFCC-266_pdp-ui-environmental-qualities
feature/motion-design-updates
feature/sfcc-873_contentful-migration-script
fix/release-v0.2.0-sit-gate-env-var-clear
release/v0.2.0
```

**Result:** 0 remote branches missing locally (63 local, 24 remote refs). Every local branch with a live upstream is now in sync — except two, below. Still on `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`, tree clean.

One correction worth making explicit: my session-start claim that this branch is 0 behind `develop` **still holds**. The stale ref was the *local* `develop` branch; `origin/develop` was already current, so PR #107 genuinely needs no rebase.

## Two branches I deliberately did not touch

Both have diverged — real local commits that exist nowhere on the remote. Merging or rebasing either is a decision that can lose work, so it's yours:

| Branch | State | Unique work |
|---|---|---|
| `f2r-component-registry` | ahead 27, behind 218 | 23 commits not in `develop` even by patch-id |
| `feature/SFCC-662-adyen-pwa-install` | ahead 11, behind 193 | 9 commits not in `develop` even by patch-id |

The counts differ because `git cherry` ignores merge commits. Nothing on either branch has already landed in `develop` under a different hash — this is genuinely unpushed work, including the Adyen install (SFCC-662) and the ZimmLogo/ZimmFlag atoms plus the token work on the f2r branch.

**A trap in that first one:** `f2r-component-registry` and `feature/f2r-component-registry` are two local branches tracking the *same* remote. The `feature/`-prefixed one is in sync and has none of those 27 commits; the bare one holds all of them. Easy to check out the wrong one and think the work vanished. Same shape with `review/SFCC-89`, which tracks the same remote as `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information`.

## Also worth knowing

**`release/v0.2.0` is live on the remote** and `projectState.md` doesn't mention it — that doc only knows v0.1.0. Its tip is a merge of [PR #102](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/102), and there's a `fix/release-v0.2.0-sit-gate-env-var-clear` alongside it. Both are now local. If you work on the release branch itself, the supervised plan-first/confirm-every-edit rules kick in.

**Cleanup I can do on your word, but didn't:**
- **30 `[gone]` branches** — remotes deleted after merge, local copies lingering (all the SFCC-855/856/860 fixes, the footer and swatches branches, etc.). `/clean_gone` handles these.
- **13 prunable worktrees** in `/private/tmp` scratchpads, left behind by past PR-review sessions. `git worktree prune` clears them.
- 7 local-only branches with no upstream at all (3 `backup/*`, `sfcc-89-wip`, `pr-70-review`, `pr-81-preview`, `feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup`) — nothing to sync, they look intentional.

Want me to run the cleanup, sort out the two diverged branches, or go back to PR #107?

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `- it's time to build

SFCC-831: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-831
SFCC-689: https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-689

FIGMA DESIGN NODES:

https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026?node-id=40003940-189295&m=dev
https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026?node-id=40002431-40590&m=dev` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #64** (ui-kit atom/molecule,
  four-file pattern, co-located recipe, render-slot wiring), **PR #59** (global-chrome component,
  co-located recipe with shared cross-file values), **PR #56** (pure token layer, no component
  change), **PR #85** (organism composing multiple molecules under a table-driven
  `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the reference for any future story that adds a variation to an existing
  organism, or builds a new one).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

Flag: missing variants or states · a design that is archived or superseded · values with no token
· the unframed tablet band left to inference · a design that contradicts an established component
· no design at all where the story implies one.

---

## Phase 2 — reuse

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a
   ready-to-paste scoped prompt.
2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

None of these skills emits machine-readable output — they all return prose for a human. If you
need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

---

## Phase 3 — the gate

This is the part that earns the skill. Produce one table, every source, every gap:

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Severity is one of:

- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot plan around it. A missing AC, an absent design, a Tier 1 file with no
  owner approval, a `scope-check` BLOCKED verdict. **Stop here.** Report and wait for Marcel.
- 🟡 **CLARIFY** — plannable, but the plan carries a stated assumption. Name the assumption
  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

Delegate to the `zm-planner` agent (Opus). Give it everything gathered — all five findings blocks,
the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

It returns: goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning) · file
manifest with tiers and owners · steps with concrete pass criteria · per-step loop configuration ·
open questions.

Write the result to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`, and write the Phase 3 gate
table to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/findings.md`.

Create the run directory if it does not exist. **Never write run state into the repo.**

---

## Phase 5 — handoff

Present to Marcel, in **"ELI5BITFEDLOTP"** (Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The Project) register — not dumbed down, but without
jargon that gets in the way. Lead with the consequence, then the mechanism, then the fix.

1. The gate table — blockers first.
2. The plan summary — scale call, step count, file count with tier breakdown.
3. Every stated assumption, gathered in one place.
4. The paths to `plan.md` and `findings.md`.

Then say plainly whether this is ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`, or what is blocking it.

**Put decisions to him one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Do not present a wall of choices
and do not bundle unrelated calls into one question.

**This skill stops here. It never invokes `zimmerMANNBuild`** — Marcel does, once he has read the
gate. Discover → report → wait for approval → and execution is a separate, deliberate act.

**Do not hand off with an unresolved 🔴.** Handing a blocked plan to the builder is how a
build burns an afternoon on the wrong thing.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never modify anything.** This skill reads, checks and plans. The only files it writes are
  under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/`. No repo file is touched — not one.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CODEOWNERS`, `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. All Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never infer squad ownership** from `squadA.md` / `squadB.md`. They contradict each other on
  PDP/PLP and are both drafts. Read `CODEOWNERS`.
- **Never present a gap as resolved because it seems minor.** Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Say what you did not check.** A source you skipped is itself a finding.
- **Provenance, not proximity.** A document living in the codebase is a downstream artifact, not
  a source. If you cannot locate the original source for a claim, flag it **provenance unknown**
  and ask. Never fabricate a source, and never fall back to citing a codebase path as one.
- **Local-only docs are never citable.** `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are
  Marcel's personal files. **They must never appear in a PR, a commit message, or a code
  comment.** Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite the repo file
  instead — that is the citable source.
- **Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full treatment. At `quick` depth,
  drop the exemplar-PR read and the blast-radius sweep, and keep the gate. Nothing too crazy,
  no overthinking.

---

## What Marcel is missing

Close every report with this section. Always, even when it is one line.

This is **not** "what I could not verify" — that is your own blind spot and it has its own home.
This is his: something he has not thought to ask about, a decision he is about to make on a stale
premise, a risk sitting just outside this task that you can see from where you are standing, or a
call that genuinely needs him rather than you. Name it, say why it needs him, and say what you
will do if he says nothing.

Write "nothing this pass" only when you have actually gone looking. This is the one section where
a blank is itself a claim.

I'll run the gate. Starting with Phase 0 position, then loading the tools I need for parallel gathering.

**Depth: `standard`** — with Figma deepened, since you've supplied 12 specific nodes.
Reading both stories first — everything else depends on knowing the subject.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_design_context
entries.description:
Get design context for a Figma node — the primary tool for design-to-code workflows. Returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual metadata that must be adapted to the target project. 

IMPORTANT: You MUST load figma-design-to-code guidance BEFORE calling this tool. Prefer the /figma-design-to-code skill if available; otherwise read the skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md MCP resource. 

NEVER call this tool without loading that guidance first — skipping it produces code that ignores the target project's existing components, design tokens, and conventions.

Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. If a URL is provided, extract the node id and file key from the URL, for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2` and the fileKey would be `:fileKey`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName then use the makeFileKey to identify the Figma Make file. Only for Figma Make files (URLs containing `/make/`), and only when calling get_design_context, assume the nodeId is `0:1`. The response will contain a code string and a JSON of download URLs for the assets referenced in the code. It will also include a screenshot of the node for context by default.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

clientLanguages.description: A comma separated list of programming languages used by the client in the current context in string form, e.g. `javascript`, `html,css,typescript`, etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which languages are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess.

clientFrameworks.description: A comma separated list of frameworks used by the client in the current context, e.g. `react`, `vue`, `django` etc. If you do not know, please list `unknown`. This is used for logging purposes to understand which frameworks are being used. If you are unsure, it is better to list `unknown` than to make a guess

forceCode.description: Whether code should always be returned, instead of returning just metadata if the output size is too large. Only set this when the user directly requests to force the code.

disableCodeConnect.description: Whether Code Connect should be used to get the design context. Only set this when the user directly requests to disable Code Connect.

skillNames.description: A comma-separated list of Figma skill names being followed, if any (e.g. "figma-design-to-code", "figma-design-to-code,figma-code-connect"). Only pass this when explicitly instructed to by skill documentation. Used for logging purposes. If the skill was loaded via a skill-content MCP resource, prefix the skill name with "resource:". (e.g. "resource:figma-design-to-code", "resource:figma-design-to-code,resource:figma-code-connect")

excludeScreenshot.description: Whether to exclude the screenshot of the design from the response. IMPORTANT: it is not recommended to exclude screenshots. Only set this to true if the user has explicitly requested it or you are trying to preserve context.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). The nodeId parameter is optional: when omitted, the tool returns a list of the top-level pages (guid + name) in the document instead of an XML dump — use this when you don't yet know which page or node to drill into. When the user has a current selection relevant to the request, the response is prepended with a "Currently selected nodes:" block listing the selection by guid and name, so you can tell whether it matches the queried nodeId. If the URL includes `node-id`, extract it and pass it as nodeId; for example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=1-2, the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, do not set nodeId; omit the field so the tool lists top-level pages. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. If the URL is of the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName then use the branchKey as the fileKey.

nodeId.description: The ID of the node in the Figma document, eg. "123:456" or "123-456". This should be a valid node ID in the Figma document. Do not pass an empty string for node_id.

fileKey.description: The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_screenshot
entries.description: Generate a screenshot for a given node or the currently selected node in the Figma desktop app. Works on Figma design files (URL path `/design/`), FigJam boards (`/board/`), and Figma Slides (`/slides/`). The optional `maxDimension` parameter (positive integer, max 65536, default 1024) caps the longer edge of the rendered PNG in pixels — increase it when you need to inspect fine detail, decrease it for thumbnails or to save context. The JSON metadata entry in the response includes both `width`/`height` (the rendered PNG size) and `original_width`/`original_height` (the node's natural canvas size before any clamping), so callers can decide whether to re-request at a higher `maxDimension`. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id. nodeId parameter is REQUIRED. Use the fileKey parameter to specify the file key. fileKey parameter is REQUIRED. If a URL is provided, extract the file key and node id from the URL. For example, if given the URL https://figma.com/design/pqrs/ExampleFile?node-id=1-2 the extracted fileKey would be `pqrs` and the extracted nodeId would be `1:2`. If the URL does not include `node-id`, ask the user for a node-specific URL. Do not pass an empty or guessed nodeId. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). By default this tool returns a short-lived URL to the screenshot plus curl instructions for downloading the PNG — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding the image inline. The `enableBase64Response` parameter defaults to `false`.   "customfield_10231": {
    "value": "1. Given a shopper lands on the EU Domestic storefront and their browser-detected language matches one of the four supported EU languages (EN, FR, IT, ES) but does not match the current EU locale URL, when the page loads on their first visit, then the language mismatch prompt is displayed automatically.
2. Given a shopper lands on the EU Domestic storefront and their browser-detected language either matches the current EU locale URL or does not match any of the four supported EU languages, when the page loads, then the language mismatch prompt is not displayed.
3. Given the prompt is displayed, when it renders, then it shows the shopper's detected language and the current storefront language with two CTAs: one to switch to their detected language and one to stay in the current language.
4. Given the shopper clicks the switch CTA, when confirmed, then the storefront redirects to the EU locale URL matching their detected language (e.g. /fr-eu/, /it-eu/).
5. Given a shopper is on any storefront other than EU Domestic, when they browse the site, then the language mismatch prompt is never triggered.

*Cookie management for language mismatch:*

# *Given* a shopper dismisses or acts on the language mismatch slide-out
*When* the interaction is complete
*Then* a required functional cookie is set in the shopper's browser suppressing the slide-out for X days
# *Given* the cookie has been set
*When* the shopper returns to the site within X days
*Then* the language mismatch slide-out is not shown, regardless of browser-detected language mismatch
# *Given* the cookie has expired (after X days)
*When* the shopper returns to the site and their browser-detected language still does not match the storefront's language
*Then* the language mismatch slide-out is shown again
# *Given* the shopper clears their browser cookies
*When* they return to the site and their browser-detected language does not match the storefront’s language
*Then* the language mismatch slide-out is shown again, as no suppression cookie is present

We can start with 7 days but needs to be able to be changed."
  }
}

input.prompt:
Read-only investigation of the repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Salesforce PWA Kit storefront, TypeScript-only under `overrides/`). DO NOT modify, create, or delete any file. Report findings only, with `path:line` evidence for every claim.

CONTEXT — the work being planned (do not implement it, just survey):
Two Jira stories. SFCC-831 builds a reusable component `global/country-language-mismatch` with TWO variants, both rendered as a **right-anchored drawer panel using "the shared drawer shell"**:
 - `variant=location-prompt` ("Location Prompt Banner"): shows shopper's IP-detected country + mismatch message + 2 CTAs (redirect to correct storefront / stay). Fires `onRedirect()`.
 - `variant=language-prompt` ("Language Prompt Banner"): shows detected browser language + current storefront locale + 2 CTAs (switch language / stay). Fires `onSwitchLanguage(locale)` and `onDismiss()`.
The component does NOT own trigger logic or redirect behaviour — it exposes callbacks and takes props.
SFCC-689 consumes the language variant on the **EU Domestic storefront only**, triggered on first visit when browser language (one of EN/FR/IT/ES) doesn't match the EU locale URL (e.g. lands on /es-eu/ but browser is French → offer /fr-eu/). Also requires a **suppression cookie** set on dismiss/act, expiring after N days (default 7, must be configurable).
Accessibility ACs require: focus trapped in the open drawer, all interactive elements keyboard-reachable, focus returned to the trigger on close, drawer announced as a dialog with an accessible name per variant, aria-label on the close icon.

ANSWER THESE, each with file:line evidence:

1. **The shared drawer shell.** Find it. I believe there is a `zimmDrawer` under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`. Give its exact path, its full prop/API surface, its exported names, its variants and sizes, whether it is right-anchored, whether it already handles focus trap / aria-modal / Esc / backdrop click, and whether it has a co-located `.css.ts` recipe and where that recipe is registered. Quote the prop type verbatim.

2. **ui-kits inventory.** Exact `ls` of `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/`, `/molecules/`, `/organisms/`. For each directory, list the files inside. I need to know precisely which building blocks already exist (buttons, text, icons, links, etc.) versus which would have to be created.

3. **Existing prior art for this feature.** Search the whole repo (including `overrides/app/`, `config/`, `worker/`, `overrides/app/request-processor.js`) for ANY existing country-mismatch, language-mismatch, geo-detection, IP-country, locale-switcher, region-selector or storefront-redirect logic. Include commented-out/stub code and TODOs. If none exists, say so explicitly.

4. **Locale / multi-site plumbing available to a consumer.** What is available to read the current site and locale? Cover `overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts` (if present), `config/sites.js`, `config/default.js`'s `SITE_LOCALES` or equivalent. Specifically: what is the **EU Domestic** site's site ID, and exactly which locales/URL prefixes does it have configured? Does `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`, `/en-eu/` (or similar) actually exist in config? Quote the config.

5. **Microcopy.** How is UI microcopy supplied? Cover `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts` and `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/`. What is the hook's signature, its fallback behaviour with no Provider, and how does a component register new copy keys? Is there a Contentful `uiCopy` content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/`?

6. **Cookie / dismissal persistence.** Does any utility already exist for setting/reading a first-party cookie or a "seen once / suppressed for N days" flag? Check `overrides/app/utils/`, hooks, and anything Didomi-related. Also report whether any Didomi consent integration exists in the repo yet at all (grep `didomi` case-insensitively across the repo) — I need to know if it is implemented or still unbuilt.

7. **Tiers and owners.** For every path you have named as likely-touched, give its protection tier and owner. Read these ONLY from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` (Tier 1), `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` (Tier 2), and `/CODEOWNERS`. **Never** read a tier from `.claude/registry/*.md` — its Tier column is a wrong derived heuristic. Quote the matching line from the rules file or CODEOWNERS for each.

8. **Nearest existing pattern to copy.** Which existing component in this repo is the closest structural precedent for "an organism/molecule with two variants driven by a prop, composed from existing atoms, with a co-located recipe"? Look especially for a table-driven `VARIATION_CONFIG` pattern (I'm told PR #85 introduced one). Give the path and quote the variant-dispatch mechanism. Also list the canonical four-file pattern used for a new ui-kit component (component, story, test, recipe) with a real example's file list.

9. **Theme registration.** Show `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — how recipes are registered and what key names look like. Quote the relevant lines.

10. **Storybook + test conventions in practice.** Find an existing `.stories.tsx` for a portal-rendered dialog/drawer (the zimmDrawer story if it exists) and show how it queries portaled content. Find an existing `index.test.tsx` for a ui-kit organism and show what it mocks.

Use `git log`/`gh pr view 85 --json files` if helpful for the VARIATION_CONFIG question. Be exhaustive on items 1, 2, 4 and 7 — those decide the plan. If something does not exist, say "does not exist" explicitly rather than guessing at a plausible path.

input.prompt:
Read-only cross-check. DO NOT modify, create, or delete any file.

Two sources:
- A: `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` — a personal, local-only build-approach handbook (Part I "the machine", Part II "the procedure", Part III "the role"). It is a DERIVED account, not the source of truth.
- B: the repo rules at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/` — specifically `overrideStyling.md`, `css.md`, `components.md`, `testing.md`, `conventions.md`, `typescript.md`.

**Where A disagrees with B, B WINS** — and you must report the disagreement explicitly as handbook staleness. That is the primary output of this task.

THE WORK THIS IS FOR (context only — do not implement anything):
Building a new reusable component `global/country-language-mismatch` for a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront. It is a **right-anchored drawer panel** with **two variants** selected by a prop (`location-prompt` and `language-prompt`), each showing a message plus two CTA buttons. It must be composed from existing ui-kit atoms, have a co-located `<name>.css.ts` theme recipe, a Storybook story, and a Vitest test. Accessibility requirements: focus trapped in the open drawer, all interactive elements keyboard-reachable, focus returned to the trigger on close, announced as a dialog with a per-variant accessible name, aria-label on the close icon. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.

DELIVER, in these sections:

1. **What the handbook says to do** for this exact shape of work. Extract and quote the relevant guidance on: creating a new ui-kit component (atom vs molecule vs organism placement), the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe pattern and where recipes get registered, token usage (`var(--zimm-*)` vs bare Chakra keys vs `textStyle`), drawer/modal/dialog components specifically, accessibility for dialogs, Storybook story requirements and categorisation, and Vitest requirements. Quote it, don't paraphrase.

2. **Disagreements between handbook and repo rules.** For each: quote A, quote B with its file and line, and state plainly which one the builder must follow (always B) and therefore what in the handbook is stale. Pay particular attention to: token syntax (`var(--zimm-*)` vs bare token keys), where a component's recipe file lives and who owns it, component folder structure and naming, and any statement about which components are or are not already overridden.

3. **Broken citations.** The handbook cites `file:line` references. Verify every citation that bears on the work described above actually still resolves in the repo — the file exists AND the cited line still contains what the handbook claims. Report each one that does not resolve, with what it claims vs what is actually there.

4. **Gaps.** What does this work need that the handbook does NOT cover at all? Specifically consider: a two-variant component driven by a prop, portal-rendered dialog testing, focus management/focus trap, cookie-based suppression/persistence, and per-variant accessible names.

Be concrete and quote both sides. Where the handbook is simply silent, say "handbook silent" rather than inventing guidance.

## 4. Locale / multi-site plumbing

### What a consumer can read

**`overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts` does not exist.** There is no override. Consumers import the base directly:

```ts
import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site';
```

— as at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:2`, `footer/index.tsx:6`, `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:4`, `recommended-products/index.tsx:136`.

**It ships untyped**, so the house pattern is a local cast. Two forms in use:

- `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:21-23`: `const { locale: siteLocale } = useMultiSite() as { locale?: { id: string } };` — with the comment *"useMultiSite ships untyped from the base SFCC package — same cast footer/index.tsx and useHeaderNav.ts already use."*
- `useCountryConfig.ts:4-7` declares a reusable `MultiSiteContext` type: `{ site?: {id, alias?}, locale?: {id, preferredCurrency?} }`.

It returns `{site, locale, buildUrl}` (`_app/index.tsx:172`).

**`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts:18-22`** is the ready-made bridge — returns the full `CountryConfig` for the active site+locale, keyed on `sfccSiteId` **and** `locale` to disambiguate the `en-GB` collision between UK and EU-English, falling back to AU. This is exactly what a mismatch detector needs, and it's Tier 4 (unlisted, plain squad ownership).

### The config chain

`config/sites.js` is a **merge of two files**, not a literal list (`config/sites.js:20-55`): `config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI-derived locale/currency, auto-generated) + `config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-maintained aliases + `sfccSiteId` override).

### EU Domestic — the answer to your specific question

**There is no single "EU Domestic site".** EU domestic is **four separate PWA sites**, each with exactly one locale, all backed by the one real SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`.

`config/sites.overlay.js:38-42`, verbatim:

```js
  // EU domestic — four single-locale PWA sites, all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr', alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it', alias: 'it-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es', alias: 'es-eu' }] },
```

`config/default.js:129-133`:

```js
      // EU domestic: one PWA site per locale prefix — all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU (see sites.js)
      ZimmermannEUen: 'en-eu',
      ZimmermannEUfr: 'fr-eu',
      ZimmermannEUit: 'it-eu',
      ZimmermannEUes: 'es-eu',
```

**So yes — `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` all exist in config**, but as **site aliases, not locale prefixes.** `config/default.js:70-78` sets `url.site: 'path'`, `url.locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`. Because each PWA site has exactly one locale and that locale is therefore its default (`sites.js:42`: `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`), `showDefaults:false` suppresses the locale segment — the URL carries the *site alias* only.

**This is the single most important structural consequence for SFCC-689: "switching language" is switching SITE, not switching locale.** `onSwitchLanguage(locale)` cannot be implemented as a locale change within one site. There is no `SITE_LOCALES` map anywhere in `config/` — I searched; the concept doesn't exist here.

`ZimmermannEU`'s SCAPI-supported locales (`config/sites.generated.js:77-104`): `en`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`. And `sites.js:34-42` carries a long comment explaining why `defaultLocale` deliberately ignores SCAPI's site-level default — *"BM's ZimmermannEU default 'en-GB' would wrongly apply to the EUfr/EUit/EUes PWA sites too, since all 4 share one real SFCC site."*

Locale→slug lookup, if you need the reverse direction: `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts:29-48` maps `en-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, en-GB, EUR}`, `fr-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, fr, EUR}`, `it-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, it, EUR}`, `es-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, es, EUR}`.

**There is no cookie utility anywhere in `overrides/`.** Grep for `document.cookie|setCookie|getCookie|js-cookie|cookies.set|cookies.get|expires=` across `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` returns **only four hits, all HTTP `Cache-Control` headers**: `overrides/app/ssr/slasTokens.ts:86`, `pages/home/index.tsx:122`, `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:238`, `pages/product-list/index.tsx:316`. **Nearest precedent is Web Storage, not cookies** — `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`.
