### Portal-rendered drawer story — `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`

`title: 'Elements/ZimmDrawer'` (`:9`). Imports test utils from **`'storybook/test'`** (`:4`) — not `@storybook/test`, not `@testing-library/user-event`.

The portal query, verbatim (`:32-40`):

```ts
  play: async () => {
    // Portal renders outside canvasElement — testing.md §Layer-2 exception. Chakra's Drawer is
    // built on its Modal primitive, which renders DrawerContent via a Portal by default, so
    // within(canvasElement) can't reach it.
    const doc = within(document.body);
    const dialog = await doc.findByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeInTheDocument();
    await expect(dialog).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'Example drawer');
  },
```

This is the **only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`** per `.claude/rules/testing.md` — and the comment citing the exception is mandatory.

Three more conventions from this file:

- **Close assertions must `waitForElementToBeRemoved`, not `queryByRole`** (`:69-73`): *"Chakra's Drawer plays a slide-out exit transition (framer-motion) before AnimatePresence actually unmounts the dialog node — an immediate `queryByRole('dialog')` assertion here catches it mid-animation, still present with a near-100% translateX."* **Your dismiss/CTA-closes-drawer stories will hit this.**

- **Assert the accessible name, not the mechanism** (`:94-97`): `findByRole('dialog', {name: 'SIGN IN'})` rather than pinning to `aria-labelledby` vs `aria-label`. Ideal for your per-variant accessible-name AC.

## 1. The shared drawer shell — `ZimmDrawer`

**Path:** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx`

**Exports:** two only — `ZimmDrawer` (named, line 184) and `type ZimmDrawerSize` (line 37). No default export. `ZimmDrawerContent` (line 111) is a file-private internal helper.

**Right-anchored: yes, structurally.** `placement="right"` at `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:206`, plus a hand-rolled framer-motion slide at `:142-146` (`initial={{x:'100%'}} animate={{x:0}} exit={{x:'100%'}}`) and `position:fixed; top:0; right:0; bottom:0` at `:146`. Not configurable — there is no `placement` prop.

**Prop type, verbatim** (`zimmDrawer/index.tsx:39-75`):

```ts
type ZimmDrawerBaseProps = {
  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
  isOpen: boolean;
  /** Called on backdrop click, Escape, and the close button (all via Chakra's Drawer). */
  onClose: () => void;
  /** Desktop/tablet width variant — see ZimmDrawerSize. Collapses to the mobile treatment
   *  below the tablet breakpoint regardless of which value is chosen — see zimmDrawer.css.ts. */
  size: ZimmDrawerSize;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  /** Text style for the title. 'large' applies heading1 (24px, uppercase, Futura Round regular);
   *  'small' applies body2Strong (14px bold). Defaults to 'large'. Only relevant when `title`
   *  is provided. */
  titleStyle?: 'large' | 'small';
  /** Element to focus when the drawer closes. Use when the trigger may not have received
   *  keyboard focus before opening (e.g. mouse click) — without this Chakra falls back to
   *  document.body and AC10 focus-return fails. */
  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
  /** Element to focus when the drawer opens. Overrides Chakra's default (first focusable element
   *  in the panel, usually the close button) — use to land focus directly on the primary input. */
  initialFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
};

/**
 * Exactly one of:
 * - `title`       — renders an inline header row (title left, close button right); the drawer's
 *                   accessible name is derived from the rendered title element automatically.
 * - `labelledBy`  — ID of an existing element that labels the drawer (e.g. ZimmPdpDrawer's own
 *                   tab header). Paired with the floating close button.
 * - `aria-label`  — explicit string label when neither a visible title nor a separate element
 *                   is available.
 */
type ZimmDrawerProps = ZimmDrawerBaseProps &
  (
    | { title: string; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label'?: never }
    | { title?: never; labelledBy: string; 'aria-label'?: never }
    | { title?: never; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label': string }
  );
```

## 4. Locale / multi-site plumbing

### What a consumer can read

**`overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts` does not exist.** There is no override. Consumers import the base directly:

```ts
import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site';
```

— as at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:2`, `footer/index.tsx:6`, `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:4`, `recommended-products/index.tsx:136`.

**It ships untyped**, so the house pattern is a local cast. Two forms in use:

- `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:21-23`: `const { locale: siteLocale } = useMultiSite() as { locale?: { id: string } };` — with the comment *"useMultiSite ships untyped from the base SFCC package — same cast footer/index.tsx and useHeaderNav.ts already use."*
- `useCountryConfig.ts:4-7` declares a reusable `MultiSiteContext` type: `{ site?: {id, alias?}, locale?: {id, preferredCurrency?} }`.

It returns `{site, locale, buildUrl}` (`_app/index.tsx:172`).

**`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts:18-22`** is the ready-made bridge — returns the full `CountryConfig` for the active site+locale, keyed on `sfccSiteId` **and** `locale` to disambiguate the `en-GB` collision between UK and EU-English, falling back to AU. This is exactly what a mismatch detector needs, and it's Tier 4 (unlisted, plain squad ownership).

### The config chain

`config/sites.js` is a **merge of two files**, not a literal list (`config/sites.js:20-55`): `config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI-derived locale/currency, auto-generated) + `config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-maintained aliases + `sfccSiteId` override).

### EU Domestic — the answer to your specific question

**There is no single "EU Domestic site".** EU domestic is **four separate PWA sites**, each with exactly one locale, all backed by the one real SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`.

`config/sites.overlay.js:38-42`, verbatim:

```js
  // EU domestic — four single-locale PWA sites, all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr', alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it', alias: 'it-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es', alias: 'es-eu' }] },
```

`config/default.js:129-133`:

```js
      // EU domestic: one PWA site per locale prefix — all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU (see sites.js)
      ZimmermannEUen: 'en-eu',
      ZimmermannEUfr: 'fr-eu',
      ZimmermannEUit: 'it-eu',
      ZimmermannEUes: 'es-eu',
```

**So yes — `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` all exist in config**, but as **site aliases, not locale prefixes.** `config/default.js:70-78` sets `url.site: 'path'`, `url.locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`. Because each PWA site has exactly one locale and that locale is therefore its default (`sites.js:42`: `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`), `showDefaults:false` suppresses the locale segment — the URL carries the *site alias* only.

**This is the single most important structural consequence for SFCC-689: "switching language" is switching SITE, not switching locale.** `onSwitchLanguage(locale)` cannot be implemented as a locale change within one site. There is no `SITE_LOCALES` map anywhere in `config/` — I searched; the concept doesn't exist here.

`ZimmermannEU`'s SCAPI-supported locales (`config/sites.generated.js:77-104`): `en`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`. And `sites.js:34-42` carries a long comment explaining why `defaultLocale` deliberately ignores SCAPI's site-level default — *"BM's ZimmermannEU default 'en-GB' would wrongly apply to the EUfr/EUit/EUes PWA sites too, since all 4 share one real SFCC site."*

Locale→slug lookup, if you need the reverse direction: `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts:29-48` maps `en-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, en-GB, EUR}`, `fr-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, fr, EUR}`, `it-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, it, EUR}`, `es-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, es, EUR}`.

Its test file covers both throw paths (`useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts:176, 191`). Any suppression-flag utility you write needs the same try/catch on read and write.

  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
  isOpen: boolean;
  /** Called on backdrop click, Escape, and the close button (all via Chakra's Drawer). */
  onClose: () => void;
  /** Desktop/tablet width variant — see ZimmDrawerSize. Collapses to the mobile treatment
   *  below the tablet breakpoint regardless of which value is chosen — see zimmDrawer.css.ts. */
  size: ZimmDrawerSize;
  children: React.ReactNode;
  /** Text style for the title. 'large' applies heading1 (24px, uppercase, Futura Round regular);
   *  'small' applies body2Strong (14px bold). Defaults to 'large'. Only relevant when `title`
   *  is provided. */
  titleStyle?: 'large' | 'small';
  /** Element to focus when the drawer closes. Use when the trigger may not have received
   *  keyboard focus before opening (e.g. mouse click) — without this Chakra falls back to
   *  document.body and AC10 focus-return fails. */
  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
  /** Element to focus when the drawer opens. Overrides Chakra's default (first focusable element
   *  in the panel, usually the close button) — use to land focus directly on the primary input. */

};

/**
 * Exactly one of:
 * - `title`       — renders an inline header row (title left, close button right); the drawer's
 *                   accessible name is derived from the rendered title element automatically.
 * - `labelledBy`  — ID of an existing element that labels the drawer (e.g. ZimmPdpDrawer's own
 *                   tab header). Paired with the floating close button.
 * - `aria-label`  — explicit string label when neither a visible title nor a separate element
 *                   is available.

type ZimmDrawerProps = ZimmDrawerBaseProps &
  (
    | { title: string; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label'?: never }
    | { title?: never; labelledBy: string; 'aria-label'?: never }
    | { title?: never; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label': string }

## 4. Locale / multi-site plumbing

### What a consumer can read

**`overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts` does not exist.** There is no override. Consumers import the base directly:

```ts
import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site';
```

— as at `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:2`, `footer/index.tsx:6`, `zimmNavItem/index.tsx:4`, `recommended-products/index.tsx:136`.

**It ships untyped**, so the house pattern is a local cast. Two forms in use:

- `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:21-23`: `const { locale: siteLocale } = useMultiSite() as { locale?: { id: string } };` — with the comment *"useMultiSite ships untyped from the base SFCC package — same cast footer/index.tsx and useHeaderNav.ts already use."*
- `useCountryConfig.ts:4-7` declares a reusable `MultiSiteContext` type: `{ site?: {id, alias?}, locale?: {id, preferredCurrency?} }`.

It returns `{site, locale, buildUrl}` (`_app/index.tsx:172`).

**`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts:18-22`** is the ready-made bridge — returns the full `CountryConfig` for the active site+locale, keyed on `sfccSiteId` **and** `locale` to disambiguate the `en-GB` collision between UK and EU-English, falling back to AU. This is exactly what a mismatch detector needs, and it's Tier 4 (unlisted, plain squad ownership).

### The config chain

`config/sites.js` is a **merge of two files**, not a literal list (`config/sites.js:20-55`): `config/sites.generated.js` (SCAPI-derived locale/currency, auto-generated) + `config/sites.overlay.js` (hand-maintained aliases + `sfccSiteId` override).

### EU Domestic — the answer to your specific question

**There is no single "EU Domestic site".** EU domestic is **four separate PWA sites**, each with exactly one locale, all backed by the one real SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`.

`config/sites.overlay.js:38-42`, verbatim:

```js
  // EU domestic — four single-locale PWA sites, all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr', alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it', alias: 'it-eu' }] },
  { id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es', alias: 'es-eu' }] },
```

`config/default.js:129-133`:

```js
      // EU domestic: one PWA site per locale prefix — all backed by SFCC ZimmermannEU (see sites.js)
      ZimmermannEUen: 'en-eu',
      ZimmermannEUfr: 'fr-eu',
      ZimmermannEUit: 'it-eu',
      ZimmermannEUes: 'es-eu',
```

**So yes — `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` all exist in config**, but as **site aliases, not locale prefixes.** `config/default.js:70-78` sets `url.site: 'path'`, `url.locale: 'path'`, `showDefaults: false`. Because each PWA site has exactly one locale and that locale is therefore its default (`sites.js:42`: `defaultLocale: locales[0].id`), `showDefaults:false` suppresses the locale segment — the URL carries the *site alias* only.

**This is the single most important structural consequence for SFCC-689: "switching language" is switching SITE, not switching locale.** `onSwitchLanguage(locale)` cannot be implemented as a locale change within one site. There is no `SITE_LOCALES` map anywhere in `config/` — I searched; the concept doesn't exist here.

`ZimmermannEU`'s SCAPI-supported locales (`config/sites.generated.js:77-104`): `en`, `en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`. And `sites.js:34-42` carries a long comment explaining why `defaultLocale` deliberately ignores SCAPI's site-level default — *"BM's ZimmermannEU default 'en-GB' would wrongly apply to the EUfr/EUit/EUes PWA sites too, since all 4 share one real SFCC site."*

Locale→slug lookup, if you need the reverse direction: `overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts:29-48` maps `en-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, en-GB, EUR}`, `fr-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, fr, EUR}`, `it-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, it, EUR}`, `es-eu`→`{ZimmermannEU, es, EUR}`.

## 10. Storybook + test conventions in practice

### Portal-rendered drawer story — `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`

`title: 'Elements/ZimmDrawer'` (`:9`). Imports test utils from **`'storybook/test'`** (`:4`) — not `@storybook/test`, not `@testing-library/user-event`.

The portal query, verbatim (`:32-40`):

```ts
  play: async () => {
    // Portal renders outside canvasElement — testing.md §Layer-2 exception. Chakra's Drawer is
    // built on its Modal primitive, which renders DrawerContent via a Portal by default, so
    // within(canvasElement) can't reach it.
    const doc = within(document.body);
    const dialog = await doc.findByRole('dialog');
    await expect(dialog).toBeInTheDocument();
    await expect(dialog).toHaveAttribute('aria-label', 'Example drawer');
  },
```

This is the **only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`** per `.claude/rules/testing.md` — and the comment citing the exception is mandatory.

Three more conventions from this file:

- **Close assertions must `waitForElementToBeRemoved`, not `queryByRole`** (`:69-73`): *"Chakra's Drawer plays a slide-out exit transition (framer-motion) before AnimatePresence actually unmounts the dialog node — an immediate `queryByRole('dialog')` assertion here catches it mid-animation, still present with a near-100% translateX."* **Your dismiss/CTA-closes-drawer stories will hit this.**
- **Stateful stories need a named component**, not an inline `render: () => { useState(...) }` (`:19-28`) — a lowercase `render` can't call hooks.
- **Assert the accessible name, not the mechanism** (`:94-97`): `findByRole('dialog', {name: 'SIGN IN'})` rather than pinning to `aria-labelledby` vs `aria-label`. Ideal for your per-variant accessible-name AC.

Story categorisation for your component: `.claude/rules/components.md` gives `Layout/` for *"Global chrome, navigation, and structural components"*. A country/language mismatch prompt is global chrome, not commerce — so `Layout/CountryLanguageMismatch`. `ZimmDrawer` itself sits in `Elements/`.

# 4. Gaps — what this work needs that the handbook does not cover

### A two-variant component driven by a prop — near-silent
The handbook's entire coverage is Play 3 (L2017–2019):
> "**Configuration variant** (a prop) vs **composition variant** (a container or slot — structurally a second component). Getting this wrong at story time produces a component that can't express what the design needs."
> "Optional fields need explicit AC for the absent case."

No guidance on *how* to type or dispatch one. B does: `typescript.md:17` ("**Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling**… rather than one type with a pile of optional fields"). The repo has a strong precedent A never mentions — `ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`: a four-member union on `variation` plus a `VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<Variation, Config>` lookup table at `:391`, whose docblock states *"every layout/visibility decision this organism makes reads from this table… adding a future variation means adding a union member above and one row here, touching no JSX."* Copy that shape.

**One live constraint neither doc covers:** no existing component drives different *copy strings* off a variant prop. `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx` states the convention — *"Microcopy (labels, button text, status messages) comes from `useUiCopy()`, not props"* — and `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:311-312` is the closest analogue (hook computes `drawerTitle`/`description`, component just renders). So the two variants' message + CTA labels should come from `useUiCopy()` keyed by variant, not be passed in. That is an inference from repo precedent, not a documented rule — worth confirming.

### Portal-rendered dialog testing — covered for Storybook, silent for Vitest
A covers the Storybook side thoroughly (§10 harness traps, §5). It says nothing about testing a portal dialog under **Vitest**, and B's carve-out is explicitly Storybook-only (`testing.md:137`). The repo has settled on mocking the shell away — `ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.test.tsx`:
```tsx
// ZimmDrawer's own import chain is covered by zimmDrawer's own tests. Mock it to a minimal
// dialog stub so this suite can assert on open/close state without a full Chakra portal environment.
vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer', () => ({ ZimmDrawer: ({isOpen, onClose, children}) => isOpen ? (<div role="dialog">…</div>) : null }))
```
then plain `screen.getByRole('dialog')`. The one counter-example that renders a real Chakra `Modal` (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx`) needs five stubs plus an `IntlProvider > ChakraProvider` wrapper. **Handbook silent on both.**

### Focus management / focus trap — one sentence, and it's the wrong sentence for this job
A's only coverage: *"**Portal + focus trap** — when `activeElement` is outside the trap, the trap must handle it rather than assume containment"* (L698) and the `:focus-visible` warning (L697). Nothing on `initialFocusRef`, `finalFocusRef`, focus return, or that Chakra already supplies the trap. B is silent too.

`ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx` already solves all three of the brief's focus requirements: `initialFocusRef` forwarded to Chakra's `<Drawer>`, `<ModalFocusScope>` for the trap, and focus return hand-rolled because of an animation interaction the docs don't mention —
> `// Chakra's FocusLock remains active during the exit animation, so any focus call made while the drawer is still mounted (rAF, close-button onClick) gets trapped and dropped.`
> `const handleCloseComplete = () => { if (finalFocusRef) finalFocusRef.current?.focus(); };`

`ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx:66-67` is the working consumer (`finalFocusRef={triggerRef} initialFocusRef={emailInputRef}`). `returnFocusOnClose` appears nowhere in the repo. `useZimmModal` is deliberately inert (*"neither ref drives behaviour any more"*) — don't reach for it.

### Cookie-based suppression / persistence — handbook silent, and no repo precedent either
Zero handbook coverage: no `cookie`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, "don't show again", or dismissal-persistence guidance anywhere in 2,538 lines. **This is a genuine greenfield decision, not a lookup.**

Repo state: no `document.cookie`, no `js-cookie`, no cookie dependency in `package.json`. Two `sessionStorage` precedents exist via the SFCC base helpers — `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:37` (`PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY`, `getSessionJSONItem`/`setSessionJSONItem`, `{intentId, timestamp}` + TTL) and `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:121` (`isRegistered ? localStorage : sessionStorage`, with a documented Safari-private-mode try/catch). **Didomi has zero code** — docs only, and `.docs/memory/projectState.md:20` lists it `Not started`. Since AGENTS.md's consent rule is fail-closed and Hard Rule 7 blocks adding a cookie library without Integration approval, the storage mechanism needs a decision before build, not during.

### Per-variant accessible names — handbook silent, already solved in the repo
A's nearest statements are 2.5.3 (*"the accessible name must *contain* the visible label"*) and the note that the ast-grep `IconButton` rule *"does not match `aria-labelledby`"*. Nothing on giving a dialog a name that varies by variant.

`zimmDrawer/index.tsx` already encodes exactly this as a three-member union — which is also A's own "two API patterns worth copying" advice (L386–390: *"Encode the a11y contract in a discriminated union so an inaccessible combination doesn't type-check"*), just never connected to drawers:
```ts
| { title: string; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label'?: never }
| { title?: never; labelledBy: string; 'aria-label'?: never }
| { title?: never; labelledBy?: never; 'aria-label': string }
```
It sets these on `dialogProps` directly because *"Chakra's `getDialogProps` always recomputes `aria-labelledby` from a `<DrawerHeader>` that never mounts here."* Its close control is `<ZimmButton variant="icon" icon="close" label="Close" />` — **hardcoded English, not localised** (contrast `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:192`, which uses `intl.formatMessage`). For an eight-storefront locale prompt that is a defect to avoid inheriting.

### Three smaller gaps
- **Right-anchoring is not a prop.** `ZimmDrawer` hardcodes `placement="right"` plus a `position: fixed; right: 0` panel and framer-motion `x: '100%'` transitions. Nothing to pass; also nothing configurable if the design ever needs otherwise.
- **Storybook category undecided.** A says title = domain; existing precedent is `Elements/ZimmDrawer` (atom) and `Commerce/Zimm*Drawer` (organisms). A global locale prompt is neither. `components.md:139` puts "Global chrome, navigation, and structural components" under `Layout/` — that's the closest fit, but neither doc names this case.
- **Requirement source unpointed.** A tells you to verify against `.docs/` but names no doc for this. It is `.docs/prd/regional.md:71-73` — "EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)… Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032)". Also relevant: `overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, whose docblock lists *"IP-detection prompt"* as an intended-but-unbuilt consumer, `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts`, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts:10`, which already earmarks its `small` (25%) size for *"Regional Storefront"* and *"Cookies"*.

**Run date:** 2026-09-11 · **Depth:** standard (Figma deepened — 12 nodes supplied)
**Verdict: 🔴 BLOCKED — 4 blockers. No plan produced. Do not hand to zimmerMANNBuild.**

- **SFCC-831** `global/country-language-mismatch — PWA Component` · In Progress · High · due 2026-09-11 · Sprint 5 · Squad-A · labels REG-014, REG-029 · epic SFCC-2 (PWA Kit Components) · **blocks** SFCC-823 + SFCC-689
- **SFCC-689** `Regional Storefronts — EU Language Mismatch Modal` · In Progress · High · due 2026-09-11 · Sprint 5 · labels REG-029/030/031/032/033 · epic SFCC-19
- **SFCC-823** `Country Mismatch Slide-Out` · **Blocked** (by SFCC-817 *IP Geolocation Routing & AU Gating*, In Refinement) · consumer of the location variant

Branch at gate time: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` (wrong branch for this work — open draft PR #107).

---

## Gate table

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confluence 04.1.6 REG-029 vs SFCC-689 AC1/AC2 vs Figma | **Trigger signal contradiction.** REG-029 (Confirmed, "source of truth"): modal shows when the customer's **GEO-IP detected country** does not match the URL language. SFCC-689 AC1/AC2: triggers on **browser-detected language** (EN/FR/IT/ES). Figma row 4 copy corroborates REG-029 — *"Abbiamo notato che ti trovi in Francia"* ("we noticed you are in France"), which is REG-031's exact prescribed format. Two of three sources say geo-IP; the ticket says browser language. | 🔴 | PO/BA decide the signal. If geo-IP, SFCC-689 inherits the SFCC-817 dependency and is not buildable end-to-end this sprint. |
| 2 | Codebase | **No geo signal exists anywhere in the repo.** `overrides/app/request-processor.js` is the untouched Salesforce example stub (its own header says so; body only strips `utm_*`/`gclid`). `worker/main.js` is a 6-line licence header. Zero hits for `cf-ipcountry`, `x-geo`, `geoip`, `ip-country` in any implementation path. `COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE` (`overrides/app/config/countries.ts:128`, **Tier 1**) exists, is documented "used by IP-detection prompt", and has **zero consumers**. | 🔴 | SFCC-817 scope + owner for the server-side geo plumbing. Or explicitly scope SFCC-831 as props-only and defer both consumers. |
| 3 | Figma (12 nodes) | **Four distinct panels in Figma; the ticket declares two variants.** 4 rows × 3 viewports = 12. Row 1 "Country Mismatch: Location Prompt Banner" (EN, store-switch, **no bag warning**). Row 2 identical name (IT, **shipping-country** framing + bag warning). Row 3 "Country Prompt Banner" / mobile "Country Banner" (IT, **store-switch** framing + bag warning). Row 4 "EU Storefront - Language Prompt Banner". Rows 1 and 2 share a name *and* identical geometry — state is not encoded in the name. | 🔴 | Designer/BA confirm which node is canonical per variant, and whether the country side is one variant or two. |
| 4 | Confluence REG-016 vs SFCC-823 AC2/AC5 vs Figma | **Second CTA contradiction on the country variant.** REG-016 (Confirmed): CTA 2 **opens the country selector** to manually change shipping country. SFCC-823 AC2/AC5: CTA 2 is **"stay on the current storefront"** and merely closes. Figma shows *both* — row 2 CTA1 is "CAMBIA IL PAESE DI SPEDIZIONE" (change shipping country), rows 1/3 are stay-on-store. The Country & Currency Selector is itself unbuilt (own drawer tab in the design system, no code). | 🔴 | PO decision. If REG-016 wins, adds a dependency on the unbuilt selector. |
| 5 | Jira (both tickets) | Cookie suppression window is literally **"X days"** in both AC sets. Emma Kirwan: *"I need to confirm the number of days… so its probably X days until confirmed otherwise."* Never confirmed. Both tickets say "We can start with 7 days but needs to be able to be changed." | 🟡 | Assumption: 7 days, as a single named exported constant. |
| 6 | Confluence REG-019 vs Jira cookie ACs | **Re-display contradiction.** REG-019 (Confirmed): slide-out shows **"on first visit only; it will not reappear once the customer has made a selection or dismissed it."** Jira cookie ACs (PO-approved 2026-09-03, i.e. later): it **does** reappear after the cookie expires. | 🟡 | Assumption: follow the later PO-approved Jira AC; PRD REG-019 needs updating. |
| 7 | Codebase | **No cookie utility exists.** Zero `document.cookie` / `setCookie` / `js-cookie` usage in `overrides/`. `js-cookie` is present only as a transitive dep of `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, **not** in `package.json` — importing it directly would depend on an undeclared transitive dep, and adding it needs integration approval (Hard Rule 7). | 🟡 | Assumption: hand-rolled ~15-line helper in `overrides/app/utils/`, `try/catch` on **read and write** (Safari private mode throws on read — see `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:30`). |
| 8 | Codebase + REG-051 | **Didomi is entirely unbuilt** — zero hits in `overrides/`, `config/`, `worker/`, `scripts/`; `@didomi/react` not installed; `DIDOMI_API_KEY` blank. The DNT placeholder modal was removed by SFCC-863. REG-051 says "Required Cookies are non-configurable", so a first-party suppression cookie is defensible as strictly necessary. | 🟡 | Assumption: proceed; record the cookie name for the future Didomi notice. Confirm rather than assume — it will be re-litigated at PR review. |
| 9 | Figma vs `zimmDrawer.css.ts` | **The shared drawer shell's geometry does not match this design at any breakpoint.** Desktop: design panel 402px @1440 (27.9%); recipe `small` = **25%** → 360px (42px narrow). Tablet: design 420px @834 (**50.4%**); `small` → 208px (212px narrow) and `tablet` → 667px. **No existing size matches ~50%.** Mobile: design panel is **content-height** (434px location / 484px language, 522px bottom gap); recipe `baseStyle` gives `calc(100% - 58px)` → ~898px panel. All comparisons are FRAME/INSTANCE boxes, so they are legitimately comparable. `ZimmDrawer` is a shared atom with **3 consumers** (`zimmPdpDrawer`, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`, `pages/product-detail`). | 🟡 | Assumption: add a new size + a content-height mobile treatment rather than editing existing values. Needs a call — it is a shared atom. |

Hard Rule 10 requires confirming scope before crossing tiers. | 🟡 | Assumption: split SFCC-831 (T3+T2) from SFCC-689 (consumer, possibly T1) into separate branches/PRs. |
| 12 | Codebase (`config/`) | **`onSwitchLanguage(locale)` is the wrong signature for this codebase.** EU domestic is **four separate PWA sites**, not one site with four locales — `config/sites.overlay.js:38-42` defines `ZimmermannEUen/fr/it/es`, each with exactly one locale, all backed by SFCC `ZimmermannEU`; `config/default.js:129-133` maps them to `en-eu`/`fr-eu`/`it-eu`/`es-eu` as **site aliases**. With `showDefaults:false`, the URL carries the site alias only. Switching language = switching **site**. There is no `SITE_LOCALES` map in `config/`. | 🟡 | Assumption: the callback carries a target site/slug, not a locale id. Freeze this before SFCC-689 consumes it. |
| 13 | Codebase + Contentful | **Translation dependency.** REG-031 requires the message in the **current URL language**. `useUiCopy`'s `value` field is localized in Contentful, so this comes free — *only if* fr/it/es entries are actually translated. Contentful staging/prod are still empty. No seed script exists for these keys (precedent: `scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs`, run by hand). | 🟡 | Who authors/translates the copy, and by when. |
| 14 | Figma | **Design copy is placeholder and partly broken.** Row 1 mixes three countries in one panel (detected UK, "currently shopping United Kingdom", "switch to US", "STAY ON AU STORE") — detected and current match, which would not even trigger a mismatch. Row 2 CTA reads **"SHIPSPEDISCI IN AUSTRALIA"** — `SHIP` + `SPEDISCI` concatenated. | 🟡 | Final copy strings from BA/design, delivered as `uiCopy` keys. |
| 15 | Confluence | **No TSD for either story.** Nearest is `SFCC-49 — Country List Configuration TSD` (453443668), which covers the country→storefront mapping this work would read. | 🟡 | Decide whether SFCC-831 needs one, or whether SFCC-49's is sufficient. |
| 16 | Confluence REG-031 | **PRD internally contradicts itself.** REG-029: modal shows on "the EU domestic storefront **only**". REG-031 closes with "This will **not** show up if accessing the EU domestic website." | 🟡 | Doc fix; read as a copy-paste error, but confirm. |
| 17 | Figma | **All values map to existing tokens — no new token needed**, so no Tier 1 foundation change. `alias/space/{100,200,400,600,800,1200,1600,2000}`, `alias/color/text/default #191919`, `alias/color/bg/page #ffffff`, `Default/h3-strong` (16/18, ls −0.12), `Default/Body 2` (14/18), `Default/Button-lg` (14/16), `alias/size/action/height/1300: 52`. Bonus: `alias/size/action/width/min: 80` **confirms** the provisional `BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG = '80px'` in `zimmButton.css.ts`. | 🔵 | — |
| 18 | Figma | Tablet band **is** framed here, at **834px** — unusual, the 768–1022 band is normally unframed. But 834 aligns to no breakpoint token (768 / 860 / 1024), so which token it drives is an inference. | 🔵 | — |

| 20 | Codebase | **`ZimmDrawer` already satisfies every a11y AC for free** — `ModalFocusScope` focus trap, `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal` via `getDialogProps()`, per-variant accessible name through a 3-member discriminated union (`title` \| `labelledBy` \| `aria-label`), `aria-label` on the close icon, Esc + backdrop close. **Caveat:** focus return only works if `finalFocusRef` is passed — FocusLock stays active through the exit animation (documented at `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:193-197`). **Defect not to inherit:** the close button's label is hardcoded English `"Close"` — wrong on a locale prompt. | 🔵 | — |

Pre-existing, not caused by this work — but copying the nearest drawer precedent inherits them. | 🔵 | — |

Kiera Rikard-Bell answered Hazel's "is this the final approved version?" with "Done!" on 2026-09-07. | 🔵 | — |

Gate written. Here's where it lands.

## 🔴 Four blockers — this is not ready to build

**Two of them stop SFCC-831 itself. Two more stop SFCC-689 on top of that.**

**1. The language prompt's trigger is contradicted by the confirmed requirement.** SFCC-689's acceptance criteria say it fires when the shopper's **browser language** doesn't match the URL. REG-029 — which its own Confluence page calls the source of truth, and which is marked Confirmed — says it fires on **GEO-IP detected country**. The Figma settles it against the ticket: the approved copy reads *"Abbiamo notato che ti trovi in Francia"* — "we noticed you are **in France**" — which is REG-031's prescribed sentence, word for word. Two sources say location, the ticket says browser language. These are different signals with different plumbing and different privacy profiles. *Consequence:* if it's geo-IP, SFCC-689 picks up the same dependency that already has SFCC-823 Blocked, and it cannot ship this sprint — despite being due today.

**2. Nothing in the codebase can detect a country.** `request-processor.js` is still the untouched Salesforce example stub — it only strips `utm_` params. `worker/main.js` is six lines of licence header. There are zero geo headers anywhere. There *is* a `COUNTRY_BY_SHIPPING_CODE` lookup in `countries.ts` documented as "used by IP-detection prompt", with **no consumers and no data source behind it**. SFCC-817, which would build this, is still In Refinement.

**3. Figma has four different panels; the ticket declares two variants.** Your 12 nodes are 4 rows × 3 viewports. Rows 1 and 2 have *identical names* and *identical geometry* — so the difference isn't discoverable from the name. When I looked inside: row 1 is English store-switch with **no bag warning**; row 2 is Italian **shipping-country** framing **with** the bag warning; row 3 is Italian **store-switch** framing with the warning; row 4 is the language prompt. *Consequence:* I can't tell you which node is the location variant, and picking wrong means building the wrong panel.

**4. The second CTA means two different things depending on which source you read.** REG-016 (Confirmed) says CTA 2 **opens the country selector**. SFCC-823 says CTA 2 **stays on the current storefront** and just closes. Figma contains both — row 2's button is "change the shipping country", rows 1 and 3 are "stay". The country selector itself doesn't exist in code yet. That's the component's public API, so it can't be left ambiguous.

## 🟡 Worth knowing before you decide

- **The prior run's open question is still open.** Your 2026-09-09 pass flagged that the location variant fires **no callback at all** on dismiss — only the language variant has `onDismiss()`. But the consumer must set the suppression cookie whenever the shopper "dismisses **or** acts on" it. There's nothing to hook. Still true.
- **The drawer shell doesn't fit the design at any breakpoint.** `zimmDrawer`'s `small` size is 25%; the design wants 402px at desktop (27.9%), **420px at tablet (50.4%)** — no existing size is close — and on mobile a **content-height panel** (434/484px) where the recipe gives a near-full-height one with a 58px strip. `ZimmDrawer` is a shared atom with three consumers, so this isn't a free change.
- **"X days" was never resolved.** Emma explicitly left the cookie window as "X days until confirmed otherwise". 7 is the working number.
- **REG-019 says the prompt never reappears**; the later PO-approved cookie ACs say it reappears after expiry. The Jira AC is newer, but the PRD is nominally the source of truth.
- **`onSwitchLanguage(locale)` won't work as specified.** EU domestic is **four separate PWA sites** (`ZimmermannEUen/fr/it/es`), not one site with four locales — the URL carries a site alias, not a locale segment. Switching language is switching *site*.
- **No cookie utility exists**, and `js-cookie` is only a transitive dependency, so using it needs integration sign-off.
- **The design copy is placeholder.** Row 1 names three different countries in one panel. Row 2's button reads "SHIPSPEDISCI" — two words fused.

## 🔵 Good news

Every Figma value maps to an **existing** token, so no Tier 1 foundation change. `ZimmDrawer` already gives you the focus trap, dialog role, per-variant accessible name and close-button label for free — all four a11y ACs. And `alias/size/action/width/min: 80` independently **confirms** the provisional `BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG = '80px'` guess in `zimmButton.css.ts`.

Full gate: [findings.md](/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-831/findings.md) — 27 rows. Your 09-09 run is preserved as `findings-2026-09-09.md`. No `plan.md`: I won't hand a blocked plan to the builder.

Also — you're on `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` with draft PR #107 open. This work needs its own branch off `develop`.

Before we dig in, here's the part I owe you that isn't in the gate table.

## What you're missing

**Both stories passed Definition of Ready with all eight boxes ticked — including "Dependencies identified" and "Design available" — and both are due today.** That's the thing underneath all four blockers. The trigger signal contradicts a signed-off requirement, the dependency that blocks the sibling story wasn't identified on this one, and the design has four panels for two variants. The DoR wasn't exercised; it was filled in. That's a process call that's yours as FED Lead, and it connects to your standing position on committing story counts while foundational stories are still blocking downstream ones. If nothing changes here, next sprint produces the same gate.

**The component and both its consumers are due the same day.** SFCC-831 sits in the PWA Kit Components epic and explicitly doesn't own trigger logic — so the intended sequence is build-component-then-consume. Same-day due dates mean they're being built in parallel against a prop contract that isn't frozen. Your 09-09 run said "the prop contract may still move"; it still can, and finding #5 (the missing dismiss callback) is exactly the kind of thing that moves it after someone's already consumed it.

**The geo-IP gap is much bigger than these two tickets, and nobody owns the file it lands in.** REG-009 (AU IP gating), REG-013 (auto-route on entry) and REG-014 (mismatch detection) all need the same server-side plumbing, and it belongs in `request-processor.js`. That file is still the Salesforce example stub, it has **no CODEOWNERS entry at all**, and `frozenFiles.md` explicitly says to *add it to Tier 1 before that work begins*. So the highest-blast-radius file in the repo is about to receive the most security-sensitive routing logic, ungated and unowned. That's an integration-lead conversation worth starting now rather than when SFCC-817 leaves refinement.

**Whoever answers blocker #1 needs to know what they're actually deciding.** If the answer comes back "browser language", that overrides a Confirmed PRD requirement — REG-029 — not just a dev question. Per the doc-integrity rule someone has to either update REG-029 or record it as a deliberate override. Worth framing that way when you route it, or you'll get a casual "yeah, browser language" and an undocumented divergence from a signed-off spec.

**Separately:** PR #107 is still draft with every check green and CodeRabbit never having reviewed it — taking it out of draft costs nothing and starts the clock. And the four confirmed-but-unposted findings from your own reviews are still unposted; that's twice this has surfaced today.

## Where do you want to start?

My read on what's most worth your time, in order: **#3 and #4** are the only two that genuinely block SFCC-831 itself and they're both one conversation with design/BA. **#1 and #2** are really SFCC-689's problem and are a PO + SFCC-817 conversation. **#10** (drawer geometry) is the one that'll quietly cost you a rebuild if it's not settled before anyone writes the recipe.

Happy to go deeper on any of them, argue the other side, or look at something I've called wrong.

Stepping back to just this card.

## What SFCC-831 actually asks for

It's a **developer-facing component story**, not a feature story. The user story is written from the developer's point of view:

> *"As a Developer, I want a reusable `global/country-language-mismatch` React component built to the Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed across storefronts to surface country and language mismatch prompts to shoppers in a consistent drawer pattern."*

**Build one component. Two variants, chosen by a prop. Both render as a right-anchored drawer panel on the shared drawer shell.**

- `location-prompt` — "Location Prompt Banner". Shows a detected country, a mismatch message, two CTAs. Consumed by SFCC-823.
- `language-prompt` — "Language Prompt Banner". Shows a detected language, the current storefront locale, two CTAs. Consumed by SFCC-689.

**The card explicitly disowns everything else.** Its own words:

> *"The component does not own the trigger logic or redirect behaviour — that is handled by the consuming stories. It exposes callbacks for each CTA action and accepts props to control which variant renders."*

So **not** in scope for this card: geo-IP detection, browser-language detection, the suppression cookie, the redirect itself, deciding when to open, `countries.ts`, `config/`, any server-side work.

**In scope:** a presentational component, its theme recipe, a story, a test. Ten ACs — four for the shared shell (slides in right-anchored, full-width on mobile with space at the bottom; backdrop/X closes without firing a CTA callback; focus trapped and returned to the trigger; announced as a dialog with a per-variant accessible name and an aria-label on close), then three per variant covering what's displayed and which callback fires.

That is a genuinely small card. Tier 3 (`ui-kits/`, both squads, no approver gate) plus one Tier 2 line to register the recipe.

## Which of my findings actually attach to *this* card

Re-sorting them against the ask, most of what I raised belongs to the consumers, not here:

**Genuinely blocks SFCC-831** — these are its visual spec and its public API, which is the whole deliverable:
- **Which Figma node is the location variant.** Four panels, two variants, and rows 1 and 2 share a name. Can't build a variant you can't identify.
- **What the second CTA does.** REG-016 says "open the country selector"; the card says "stay on current storefront". That's the component's API, not a consumer detail.

**Shapes the API, needs deciding here** — cheaper now than after SFCC-689 consumes it:
- **No dismiss callback on the location variant** (your 09-09 finding). The consumer must set a cookie on "dismisses or acts on", and has nothing to hook.
- **`onSwitchLanguage(locale)` is the wrong shape** — EU languages are four separate *sites*, not locales within one.
- **AC8 says display the "detected browser language"; the Figma displays the detected *country*** ("we noticed you are in France"). Even though this card doesn't own the trigger, it owns the string on screen — so the trigger argument leaks in through the prop name and the rendered text.

**Affects the build but isn't a spec question:**
- **The drawer shell doesn't fit at any breakpoint** — especially tablet (design wants ~50%, no existing size is close) and mobile (design wants a content-height panel, the recipe gives near-full-height).

**Belongs to SFCC-689/823, not here:** the geo-IP trigger signal, the absent geo plumbing, the cookie window, the Didomi question, REG-019's never-reappear rule, the Contentful translations.

So the honest position: **this card is about 80% unblocked.** Two design/PO answers and three API decisions stand between it and a build. The scary-looking half of the gate is the consumers' problem, not this one's.

Want me to go through those two design questions in detail — specifically what I'd need from Hazel or Kiera to name the canonical location node?

Verified. Here's the component-wise answer.

## Reused unchanged — and it's a clean fit

| Piece | What it covers | Match |
|---|---|---|
| `ZimmDrawer` (atom) | Panel, backdrop, floating close X, focus trap, `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal`, Esc + backdrop close, focus return | Covers all 4 shared-shell ACs with no code |
| `ZimmButton` (atom) | Both CTAs — `variant="secondary"` (outline) and `variant="primary"` (dark), `size="large"`, `fullWidth` | **Exact.** `size="large"` → 52px height, 80px min-width, 14px/500/lh16 label. Figma asks for `action/height/1300: 52`, `action/width/min: 80`, `Default/Button-lg` 14/500/16 |
| `textStyle="heading3"` | The uppercase heading | **Exact.** 16px / 500 / lh18 / ls −0.12 / uppercase. Figma `Default/h3-strong` is 16 / 500 / 18 / −0.11999. The file even comments it `ZIM/h3-strong` |
| `textStyle="body2"` | The body paragraph | **Exact.** 14px / 400 / lh18 / ls 0. Figma `Default/Body 2` identical |
| `useUiCopy` | The copy strings, per variant | Degrades to inline fallbacks with no Provider, so it works in stories and tests with zero setup |

So: **no new atoms, no new tokens, no typography work.** The panel is only ever heading + paragraph + two stacked buttons — no icons, no inputs, no accordions, no images.

## What's actually new — four files and one line

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/
  index.tsx                              ← the organism
  zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts     ← co-located recipe (layout only)
  index.stories.tsx                      ← Layout/ category
  index.test.tsx                         ← render-branch + callback wiring
```

plus one import and one key in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (the only Tier 2 touch).

**`index.tsx`** — a discriminated union on `variant`, dispatched through a `VARIATION_CONFIG` lookup table rather than `if`/`switch` in the JSX, following `zimmProductCard` from PR #85. Purely presentational: `isOpen` and `onClose` are props, so **no internal state and no hook** — the consumer owns all of that.

**One API detail worth deciding now:** the design has *no* header row — the close X floats top-right and the heading sits well below it in the content area. So this should use `ZimmDrawer`'s `labelledBy` form, pointing at the heading's own `id`, **not** its `title` prop (which renders a title-left/close-right header row the design doesn't have). That's also what satisfies AC4's "accessible name matching the active variant" for free — the visible heading becomes the dialog's name, so it changes with the variant automatically.

**The recipe** is layout only: content padding, the gap between heading/body/actions, and the button stack spacing. Every value as `var(--zimm-*)` — a bare token key fails `recipeGuards.test.ts` and breaks the build.

## The one place "just reuse the drawer" doesn't hold

Desktop is fine. Tablet and mobile aren't:

- **Tablet:** `ZimmDrawer`'s `small` is 25% at every width above the mobile breakpoint. The design wants **420px of 834 ≈ 50%**. Nothing in the size scale is close (`small` → 208px, `tablet` → 667px).
- **Mobile:** the shell's base style is `calc(100% − 58px)` — a near-full-height panel with a thin strip of backdrop. The design wants a **content-height** panel: 434px for location, 484px for language, in a 956px viewport.

That mobile one is the substantive difference, and it's also exactly what AC1 describes — "full width on mobile **with space at the bottom**." The design's "space at the bottom" is ~522px; the shell gives 58px, because it was measured against the PDP drawer, whose content is long.

So there's a fifth thing to build, and it's a decision rather than a task: either add a size to `zimmDrawer.css.ts` and widen the `ZimmDrawerSize` union, which touches a shared atom with three live consumers (`zimmPdpDrawer`, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`, `pages/product-detail`) — or override width/height from the new component, which means fighting `ZimmDrawer`'s own `content` recipe part from outside. The first is cleaner; the second is contained but fragile.

My read: add a new named size to the shell. It's additive, the three existing consumers keep their current size strings untouched, and the file already anticipates exactly this — it has an unused `xLarge` sitting there for Cart on the same reasoning.

Want me to pin down the tablet/mobile numbers properly against the design system's own `pdp/drawer` size set before you decide?

content.text:
Verified the whole chain. Here's the Contentful picture.

## Strictly: SFCC-831 has zero Contentful deliverables

Nothing in the description or any of its 10 ACs mentions Contentful, content authoring, or a content type. The ACs cover drawer behaviour, accessibility, what's displayed, and which callback fires. That's it.

**And no schema work is needed either.** The `uiCopy` content type already exists (`scripts/contentful/content-types/uiCopy.js`) and is explicitly designed so that *"adding a new string never requires a schema change"* — `key` → `value` pairs, fetched in bulk. So the Tier 2 `content-types/` directory stays untouched.

## What the card *does* own: the keys and their fallbacks

The repo convention makes copy Contentful's job — `zimmSubscribeSection` states it outright: microcopy comes from `useUiCopy()`, not props. So SFCC-831 owns **naming the keys and writing the English fallbacks in code**. It does *not* own seeding the entries or translating them — those are content tasks belonging to the consumers or a separate content ticket.

**Contentful is not a blocker.** `useUiCopy` is `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`, so the component renders, the stories work, and the tests pass with Contentful entirely absent. You can build and merge this card with zero Contentful entries in existence.

## The part that's a real decision on this card

Almost nothing in the design is a static string — nearly every line carries runtime data. So these are **templates**, and `t(key, fallback, values)` supports `{token}` interpolation:

```
"Looks like you're in {detectedCountry}"
"Welcome to Zimmermann Europe. We noticed you're located in {detectedCountry},
 would you like to view our site in {targetLanguage}?"
"Switch to {targetStore} store"  /  "Stay on {currentStore} store"
```

**And the design already demonstrates why naive interpolation breaks in French, Italian and Spanish:**

- Row 3's CTA reads **"PASSA AL NEGOZIO SAN MARINO"** while its own body text correctly says *"al negozio **di** San Marino"*. The CTA lost the preposition — that's a `{country}` token dropped into a slot that needed a connecting word.
- Row 2's CTA reads **"SHIPSPEDISCI IN AUSTRALIA"** — an English template and an Italian one fused.

Romance languages inflect: the article and preposition change with the noun's gender and initial sound. `"in {language}"` survives ("in francese", "in italiano"), but country names don't — "di Francia", "dell'Italia", "degli Emirati". One `{country}` token cannot carry that.

So the modelling call, worth making *before* the keys are named: either **per-locale full-sentence keys** (no inflected noun ever interpolated), or **a name table storing the correctly-inflected phrase per locale** rather than the bare country name. The first is more keys and more translation; the second is a small data structure someone has to own. Either way it changes the key count and who authors them.

## Two constraints worth knowing

**1. `value` is a `Symbol`, not `Text` — hard 256-character cap, single line, no rich text.** The longest string in the design is ~148 characters, so it fits — but with a long country name interpolated there's less headroom than it looks, and there's no line-break capability if design ever wants one.

**2. An untranslated string silently renders in English.** I checked the space bootstrap: `fr`, `it`, `es` are all declared `optional: true` with `fallbackCode: 'en'`. So a missing Italian value doesn't error and doesn't show the raw key — it quietly serves English. For a prompt whose entire purpose is REG-031 *("display the modal message in the language of the current storefront URL")*, that's a requirement failing invisibly. Worth a content checklist or a test, because nothing will tell you.

## Good news on the plumbing

**The locale chain is already correct and needs no work.** I verified both ends:

- `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:22-25` passes `siteLocale.id` from `useMultiSite()` straight to the CDA call.
- `bootstrapSpace.mjs:40-51` declares `fr`, `it`, `es` with a comment confirming the intent: *"codes match SFCC sites.js locale IDs exactly so no mapping is needed."*

So EU-Italian site → `locale: 'it'` → Italian value. No mapping layer to build. (One small oddity: `CONTENTFUL_FALLBACK_LOCALE` is `'en-US'` in code while the space default is `'en'` — harmless, since `en-US` exists and falls back to `en`, but they're not the same thing.)

**Seeding precedent exists:** `scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs` (SFCC-742, 8 entries, idempotent, `--target <env>`). Copy that shape when the keys are settled. Note it's run by hand — not wired into `package.json`.

## The open Contentful question — and it's not this card's

Whether the **live** space actually has `fr`/`it`/`es` provisioned, and whether anyone has authored the values. The bootstrap *declares* them, but declaring isn't provisioning — the same gap that left `en-CA` unconfirmed. And staging/prod were still empty as of the last check.

That's SFCC-689's problem, not SFCC-831's. But someone needs to own authoring and translating this copy, and right now nobody does — which is the finding I'd take to Jasmijn rather than solve in code.

content.text:
Checked both paths. The answer is cleaner than I expected, and there's a trap.

## How Contentful copy gets translated

**Documented position — `.docs/prd/regional.md:115`:**

> *"Translation pipeline (REG-047, de-scoped 2026-05-25): the end-to-end configurable pipeline requirement was withdrawn. Translation occurs directly between **Contentful and Transperfect** outside the PWA Kit's concern; any SFCC-held strings are translated via static JSON files. **No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads.**"*

So yes — TransPerfect, and it's **out-of-band**. `architecture.md:247` classes it as integration mode "Out-of-band": *"Translated copy lands in Contentful via vendor workflow."* The PWA never calls TransPerfect. You author the English value, TransPerfect fills the `fr`/`it`/`es` values in the same entry, and `uiCopyProvider` picks them up because `value` is a localized field.

**And `uiCopy` was purpose-built for this.** Its `description` field exists for exactly this reason — from the content type itself:

> *"Translator/editor context — not localized… Translators working key-by-key in **Transperfect** can't see the string in situ on the page."*

That's a strong signal: whoever designed the content type was already planning for TransPerfect doing key-by-key translation. So fill in `description` for every key you add — it's the only context the translator gets, and for this component the context matters enormously (see the inflection problem below).

**What's genuinely unresolved: the trigger.** Nobody has defined how a new or changed string reaches TransPerfect and comes back. `architecture.md:247` says "Translation workflow trigger TBD". `projectState.md` lists "Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD)" as an unresolved dependency. And the requirement that *would* have specified it — REG-047 — was withdrawn, so no requirement owns it. There's also **no TransPerfect doc in `.docs/integration/`** (18 docs, none for it); `integration/index.md` pushes it to the MuleSoft middleware design and out of PWA scope.

So the mechanism is agreed and needs no FE work; the operational trigger is unowned. For SFCC-831 that's fine — you author English and the entries sit there — but nobody can currently tell you *when* the Italian arrives.

## No — it's not one string

Per panel the design has four: heading, body paragraph, CTA 1 label, CTA 2 label. Times four EU locales (`en-GB`, `fr`, `it`, `es`):

| | Keys | Localized values |
|---|---|---|
| Language variant | 4 | 16 |
| Location variant | 4 (×1 panel) | 16 |
| **If the country side resolves to one panel** | **~8** | **~32** |

And if the inflection problem forces per-target full sentences instead of `{country}` interpolation, the body line alone multiplies: one sentence per (current locale × target locale) pair — 4 × 3 = **12 sentences for one line**. That's the cost of the modelling decision I flagged last turn, expressed in translation units.

## The trap: the other translation surface is a dead end

This repo has **two** translation paths, and they're in very different states.

**Path 1 — Contentful `uiCopy`** → TransPerfect, out-of-band, business-editable, no deploy. Designed for translation. ✅

**Path 2 — react-intl `translations/*.json`** → I tested it. Take a real Zimmermann-authored key, `gallery_overlay.trigger.close` from `zimmGalleryOverlay`:

```
en.json      MISSING
en-GB.json   MISSING
fr.json      MISSING
it.json      MISSING
es.json      MISSING
```

It's in **no catalogue at all — not even English.** And the extraction script only ever targets English:

```
extract-default-translations -> extract-default-messages.js en-US en-GB
```

`fr.json`, `it.json`, `es.json` are all dated 9 July — untouched upstream Salesforce files containing only base-template strings. **No Zimmermann-authored string has ever been translated into an EU language by any mechanism**, and nothing in the pipeline would send them to TransPerfect.

**So the consequence for this card:** if SFCC-831's copy goes through `useIntl`, it renders in English on the Italian storefront forever and REG-031 fails silently. If it goes through `useUiCopy`/Contentful, it's on the only path that actually reaches a translator.

**Put the copy in Contentful `uiCopy`.** That's the repo convention anyway, but the translation picture makes it not a preference — it's the difference between translatable and not.

## One thing that can't be translated as written

`ZimmDrawer`'s close button is hardcoded `label="Close"` — English, in neither translation surface. Every consumer inherits it. On a panel whose entire purpose is speaking to the shopper in their own language, an English "Close" in the corner is the one visible thing you can't fix from this card without touching the shared atom.

That's worth deciding alongside the drawer-size question, since both are the same shared-atom change: add a `closeLabel` prop (or route it through `useUiCopy` inside `ZimmDrawer`) while you're in there for the size.

Want me to work out what the key set and `description` entries would actually look like, so you've got something concrete to hand Jasmijn for the copy and TransPerfect brief?

content.text:
## The short version

**Four new files, one line in an existing file, and about eight copy keys. That's the whole card.**

Everything that sounds hard about this story — geo-detection, cookies, redirects, translation pipelines — is explicitly somebody else's card. This one builds a panel that takes props and renders.

---

## What you actually ship

**1. One new component folder** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/`

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `index.tsx` | The organism. Two variants via a discriminated union on `variant`, dispatched through a `VARIATION_CONFIG` table (the `zimmProductCard` pattern). Wraps `ZimmDrawer`, puts a heading + paragraph + two `ZimmButton`s inside. No state, no hook, no fetching. |
| `zimmCountryLanguageMismatch.css.ts` | The recipe. Layout only — content padding, the gaps, the button stack. Every value a `var(--zimm-*)`. |
| `index.stories.tsx` | `Layout/` category. `Default` plus one per variant. A `play` for close + CTA wiring, querying `document.body` because the drawer portals out of the canvas. |
| `index.test.tsx` | Mock `ZimmDrawer` to a dialog stub, mock `ZimmIcon`, mock `useUiCopy`. Assert the right branch renders per variant and the right callback fires per CTA. |

**2. One line in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`** — an import and a key. This is the card's only Tier 2 touch.

**3. Around eight copy keys** — `useUiCopy` calls with English fallbacks, plus a `description` for each so the TransPerfect translator has context. The keys live in code; the Contentful entries are a separate content task and the component renders fine without them.

---

## What you are explicitly *not* building

This is the part worth being loud about, because the gate made this card look scarier than it is:

No IP or geo detection. No browser-language detection. No cookie. No redirect. No `countries.ts` or `config/` change. No Contentful schema change. No new design tokens. No new atoms. No hook. No `translations/*.json` work.

`ZimmDrawer` and `ZimmButton` are reused unchanged, and `textStyle="heading3"` / `textStyle="body2"` match the Figma type styles **exactly** — I checked the numbers on both sides.

---

## The one deliverable that's a decision, not a task

**The drawer shell doesn't fit the design at tablet or mobile.** Tablet wants ~50% of an 834px viewport; `ZimmDrawer`'s `small` gives 25%. Mobile wants a panel sized to its content (434/484px) with a big gap below; the shell gives a near-full-height panel with a 58px strip.

*Consequence:* build it as-is and the panel is visibly wrong on two of three breakpoints — a guaranteed review comment or a QA defect.

*Mechanism:* the size lives in `zimmDrawer.css.ts` as a variant, and the size names are a union type in `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`. Both are a shared atom with three live consumers.

*Fix:* add a **new** named size rather than changing an existing one. Additive, so `zimmPdpDrawer`, `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer` and the PDP page keep their current behaviour untouched. The file already does exactly this — it carries an unused `xLarge` size for Cart on the same reasoning.

While you're in that file, the close button's hardcoded English `label="Close"` is the one string on this panel that can't be translated. Same file, same change — worth doing together rather than twice.

---

## What still stops you starting

**Two answers from design/BA:**
1. **Which Figma node is the location variant?** There are three country panels with two different names and three different CTA pairings. Not a preference — you can't build a variant you can't identify.
2. **What does the second CTA do?** REG-016 says "open the country selector"; the ticket says "stay on this storefront". That's the component's public API.

**Three decisions you can make yourself, but should make now rather than after SFCC-689 consumes it:**
3. Does a dismiss callback fire on *every* close path? (Right now only the language variant has one, and the consumer needs it to set the cookie — your own 09-09 finding.)
4. `onSwitchLanguage(locale)` needs reshaping — EU languages are four separate *sites*, not locales within one site.
5. Does the language panel display a detected **language** (what AC8 says) or a detected **country** (what the approved Figma copy says)? That changes the prop name and the sentence on screen.

---

**Net:** roughly a day's build once #1 and #2 come back. The card is small; the confusion around it isn't its own fault — it inherited it from two consumer stories that are genuinely blocked.

Want me to draft #1 and #2 as a short, citable message to Hazel and Jasmijn so you can send it and unblock the rest today?

content.text:
Confirmed — SFCC-689 is the only card carrying any Language Modal requirement, and two of them aren't on it. Here's the card.

## What SFCC-689 asks for

Where SFCC-831 is the panel, **689 is the behaviour.** It's the container story: decide when the panel opens, feed it, handle its buttons, and remember that the shopper dealt with it.

> *"As a Shopper browsing the EU Domestic storefront, I want to be prompted to switch to my preferred language when my detected language does not match the EU URL I have landed on, so that I can shop in the language most relevant to me."*

Its own description is explicit about the split: *"The underlying PWA component… is built in SFCC-831 and consumed here."* There's a formal Jira "is blocked by" link to match.

**Six pieces of actual work:**

1. **Detect** the shopper's language — or country (that's the blocker, below)
2. **Compare** it against the language of the EU site they landed on
3. **Map** the detection to a target EU site (`/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`)
4. **Gate** it — EU Domestic only, and only for the four supported languages
5. **Persist** the dismissal — a cookie, 7 days, changeable
6. **Wire** it — mount the panel, pass the props, handle switch vs stay, perform the redirect

**Scope fence:** AC5 says it never triggers on any storefront other than EU Domestic. Worth remembering that "EU Domestic" is **four separate PWA sites** (`ZimmermannEUen/fr/it/es`), so the gate is "am I on any of those four", and the comparison is against whichever one you're on.

## Where it diverges from the confirmed requirements

This is the card's real problem, and it's bigger than SFCC-831's.

**The trigger signal.** AC1/AC2 say **browser-detected language**. REG-029 (Confirmed) says **GEO-IP detected country**. The approved Figma copy backs REG-029 — *"we noticed you are in France"*. 🔴

**REG-030 is keyed differently from AC4.** REG-030 maps **countries** to locales: France *and Monaco* → `/fr-eu/`, Italy *and San Marino* → `/it-eu/`, Spain → `/es-eu/`. That's **five countries into three locales**. AC4 maps **detected language** to a locale — four languages into four sites. These aren't the same shape, and Monaco and San Marino only exist as concepts in the country version. You cannot satisfy REG-030 from a browser-language signal.

**REG-031 specifies the sentence, and it names a country.** *"we noticed you're located in [detected country]"*, rendered in the current URL's language. AC3 instead says the panel shows "the detected **language** and the current storefront language". The Figma follows REG-031.

So all three of these collapse into one question: **country or language?** Answer it and REG-030/031 fall into place. Leave it and every one of the five ACs is subtly wrong.

**And if the answer is country, this card is blocked exactly like SFCC-823** — it needs the IP geolocation work in SFCC-817, which is still In Refinement, and there is no geo plumbing anywhere in the repo today.

## The design link on this card points at the wrong panel

SFCC-689's Design field is Figma node `40002218-52405`. I pulled its metadata: that's **"Country Mismatch: Location Prompt Banner"** — the *other* variant. Hazel added it on 09-09 with the note *"already got the design from the corresponding PWA component story"*, copying it across from SFCC-831.

The actual Language Prompt Banner nodes are `40002431-40586` (desktop), `40003940-189295` (tablet), `40002431-40590` (mobile). Small thing, easy fix, but right now anyone opening this ticket's design link builds the wrong panel.

## Three gaps with nobody's name on them

**REG-034 and REG-035 are Confirmed requirements that no Jira card carries.** I searched — SFCC-689 is the only story with any Language Modal label, and it has REG-029 through 033 only.

- **REG-034**: don't show the modal for shoppers in countries with no dedicated EU locale, and offer `/en-eu/` as the default instead. AC2 partially covers the "don't show" half; the `/en-eu/` default is unaddressed.
- **REG-035**: apply the logic consistently *"regardless of entry point, including Instagram, Google Shopping feeds, direct URL entry, and organic search."* Nothing on this card mentions entry points, and it has teeth — see next.

**No AC says the redirect preserves the current page.** A shopper who deep-links from Google Shopping to a product on `/es-eu/` and taps "view in French" should land on **that same product** on `/fr-eu/`, not the French homepage. Because these are four separate sites, that's a deliberate cross-site URL build, not a locale swap — it won't happen by accident. REG-035 implies it matters; no acceptance criterion asks for it.

**The cookie ACs have no requirement behind them.** REG-029–035 contain nothing about persistence — REG-019's "first visit only, never reappears" belongs to the *country* slide-out. Jasmijn added the cookie block to this card by adapting SFCC-823's, and Emma PO-approved it. That's legitimate, just be aware it's a card-level decision with no requirement ID, and the window is still literally "X days".

## Net

SFCC-831 is small and nearly ready. **SFCC-689 is the one that's genuinely stuck** — one answer (country or language) decides three of its five ACs, its requirement mapping, and whether it depends on unbuilt server-side work that belongs to a different story. It's due today and it cannot be finished today.

The cheapest useful thing: get the country-or-language answer. Want me to draft that question with the specific citations — REG-029, REG-030's country list, and the Figma copy — so it's a decision rather than a discussion?

content.text:
**Yes — but it's narrower than "EU storefronts".** It's EU **Domestic** only.

## The distinction that matters

There are two EU storefronts, and only one gets the prompt:

| Storefront | Sites / locales | Language prompt? |
|---|---|---|
| **EU Domestic** | 4 PWA sites — `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` · SFCC checkout · EUR | ✅ Yes |
| **EU International** | `ZimmermannEUIntl` — `/en-ch/` · Global-e checkout | ❌ No |

EU International is excluded because it's **English-only**. REG-043 gives it a single locale (`en-CH`), and REG-044 says *"All other storefronts will serve content in English only."* One language means there's no mismatch to detect.

All three sources agree, so this one isn't ambiguous:
- **REG-029:** *"on the EU domestic storefront **only**"*
- **SFCC-689 description:** *"the EU language mismatch prompt on the EU Domestic storefront only"*
- **SFCC-689 AC5:** any storefront other than EU Domestic → never triggered

## The asymmetry with the other prompt

Worth holding in mind, because it changes how widely SFCC-831 gets consumed:

- **Location/country prompt** — REG-014 through 019 all say Storefront = **"ALL (excl. AU)"**. That's 7 of 8 storefronts. AU is excluded because it's IP-gated at the routing level (REG-009).
- **Language prompt** — EU Domestic's four sites only.

So the component lands almost everywhere; only its language variant is EU-scoped.

## How the gate should actually be written

Here's the neat part. All four EU Domestic PWA sites share **one** SFCC site id:

```js
{ id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
{ id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr',    alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
{ id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it',    alias: 'it-eu' }] },
{ id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es',    alias: 'es-eu' }] },
```

So the gate is **one** comparison — `site.sfccSiteId === 'ZimmermannEU'` — not a four-way list. These are the only sites in the whole config with an `sfccSiteId` override; every other site omits it entirely, and EU International is plain `ZimmermannEUIntl`. So it excludes itself naturally.

## One thing I found while checking this — and it's the hook 689 would reach for

`useCountryConfig()` is **broken on exactly these four sites.**

It does `c.sfccSiteId === site?.id` — comparing the config's SFCC id (`ZimmermannEU`) against the PWA site id (`ZimmermannEUfr`). Those never match, so on all four EU Domestic sites it silently falls through to the **AU** default: AU currency, AU checkout owner, AU everything.

*Why nobody's noticed:* its test mocks `site: { id: 'ZimmermannEU' }` — a value `config/sites.js` **cannot emit**, since it puts the PWA id in `id` and the SFCC id in a separate `sfccSiteId` field. The test encodes the wrong assumption, passes, and hides the runtime failure.

*How bad:* latent, not live — nothing in production consumes the hook yet. But the footer's comment cites it as *"the existing precedent for this exact lookup"* and states `site.id` is *"the resolved SFCC site ID"*, which is wrong. The footer itself is fine, because the Contentful region seeder writes **PWA** site ids (`ZimmermannEUfr`), matching what the footer passes. So: working code, wrong comment, spreading a wrong belief.

*The fix is one line:* `c.sfccSiteId === (site?.sfccSiteId ?? site?.id)`, plus correcting the test mocks to real site ids and fixing the footer comment.

I've flagged it as a separate task so it doesn't get lost in the SFCC-689 work.

input.title: Fix useCountryConfig EU site resolution
input.tldr: While scoping the EU language mismatch story I found useCountryConfig silently returns the Australian config on all four EU Domestic storefronts, and its test hides this by mocking a site ID the config can never produce. A new session would fix the comparison, correct the test, and clean up a misleading comment in the footer that repeats the same wrong assumption.
input.prompt:
Fix a latent site-resolution bug in `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` in the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa).

THE BUG
`useCountryConfig()` resolves the active region with:

    const match = Object.values(COUNTRIES).find((c) => c.sfccSiteId === site?.id && c.locale === locale?.id);

`site` comes from the base SFCC `useMultiSite()`, whose site object is built by `config/sites.js`. That file emits `{ id, sfccSiteId?, l10n }` — `id` is the **PWA site id** and `sfccSiteId` is a **separate field**, present only on the four EU Domestic sites:

    { id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
    { id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr',    alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
    { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it',    alias: 'it-eu' }] },
    { id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es',    alias: 'es-eu' }] },

`overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` gives all four EU slugs `sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'`. So the comparison is `'ZimmermannEU' === 'ZimmermannEUfr'` → false on every EU Domestic site, and the hook falls through to `COUNTRIES[DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG]` (AU) — wrong currency, wrong checkoutOwner, wrong globalEPricing. Every other storefront works, because those sites have no `sfccSiteId` override so `id` and `sfccSiteId` coincide.

WHY IT'S NOT CAUGHT
`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.test.ts` has a `mockSite(siteId, localeId)` helper that sets `{ site: { id: siteId } }`, and the four EU tests pass `'ZimmermannEU'` as that id — a value `config/sites.js` can never emit. The tests pass while the runtime path fails.

SCOPE OF WORK
1. Fix the comparison in `useCountryConfig.ts` to prefer the explicit SFCC id and fall back to the PWA id, e.g. `c.sfccSiteId === (site?.sfccSiteId ?? site?.id)`. Widen the local `MultiSiteContext` type to include `sfccSiteId?: string` on `site`.
2. Fix the test: `mockSite` should set a realistic site object (`{ id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU' }`) for the EU cases, so the suite exercises what `config/sites.js` actually produces. **Make the corrected test fail against the current implementation first, to prove it covers the bug**, then apply the fix.
3. Fix the misleading comment in `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` (~line 194-196). It claims `site.id` "is the resolved SFCC site ID — confirmed against useCountryConfig.ts's identical client-side pattern". That is wrong: `site.id` is the PWA site id. The footer's own behaviour is CORRECT and must not change — it passes `site.id` into `pickMostSpecificByRegion`, and `scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs` seeds Contentful `region.siteId` with PWA site ids (`ZimmermannEUen`/`EUfr`/`EUit`/`EUes`/`EUIntl`), so they match. Only correct the comment so it stops propagating the wrong belief.

CONSTRAINTS
- `overrides/` is TypeScript only. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test` before finishing.
- Do NOT modify `config/` or `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` / `countries.generated.ts` — `config/` is Tier 1 absolute and `countries.ts` is Tier 1 (see `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`). The fix belongs entirely in the hook, its test, and the footer comment.
- `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` is Tier 4 (unlisted); `overrides/app/components/footer/` is Tier 2 (Global Shell, both squads) — a comment-only change there is fine but note it in the PR.
- Start from a new branch off `develop` (`fix/usecountryconfig-eu-site-resolution`). Do not commit or push without being asked.

content.text:
Flagged as a standalone task — there's a chip you can kick off in its own worktree whenever.

Back to your question: **EU Domestic only, all four of its language sites, and not EU International.** The gate is a single `sfccSiteId === 'ZimmermannEU'` check, which is genuinely the tidiest part of this whole story.

The thing that follows from it, and that's worth deciding before 689 gets built: **REG-030's mapping only has three destinations** — France/Monaco → `/fr-eu/`, Italy/San Marino → `/it-eu/`, Spain → `/es-eu/`. Nothing maps *to* `/en-eu/`. So an English-speaking shopper who lands on `/it-eu/` has no defined target, and REG-034 says don't show them the prompt at all — they just get `/en-eu/` as a default "alternative" without being asked.

That means the prompt is effectively a **three-destination** feature on a four-site storefront, and `/en-eu/` is a one-way door: you can be sent away from it, never to it. If that's intentional, fine — but it's the kind of thing that reads as a bug in UAT when someone on `/it-eu/` with an English browser sees nothing happen.
